implementation_notes: Xcode projects carry their own anchor class: build phases referencing files and resources that are no longer compiled, and Copy Bundle Resources entries for assets nobody uses. Both are invisible in Swift and are exactly the case the boat-anchor discussion names when it describes a developer removing unused 3D assets from a 2D build. Swift's compiler also warns on unused variables and on `@objc` selectors never called from Objective-C, and Swift Package Manager's `unused dependency` output (from `swift package show-dependencies` plus an audit) covers the dependency half. Preview and test targets can keep files alive that the app target no longer uses.
idiom_name: unused target file, unused asset, unused `@objc` selector
pitfalls: A file still listed in a build phase is compiled even if no code references it, so removing the code is not enough.
Resources copied into the bundle cost bundle size and are never linked, so no tool will flag them.
An asset catalogue entry referenced by a localised string name only in a storyboard is live with no code reference.
